Subject: MSA redlines — IP infringement liability exception

Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal reviewed the draft MSA and we have one substantive open item that will block signature: the liability cap carve-out for intellectual property infringement. Our procurement counsel attached a redline (Acme_MSA_redlines_2026-04-20.pdf) that includes the following request:

- Add explicit language that claims for third-party IP infringement and Redwood's indemnity obligations for such claims are not subject to the general liability cap or, alternatively, are subject to a higher cap (we propose uncapped or a higher multiple).
- Clarify that remedies for proven IP infringement include injunctive relief and recovery of consequential losses where those losses directly flow from the infringement (we can provide examples).

Acme's rationale: our customers may be downstream licensees and a successful third-party claim could cause outsized business disruption; we need the vendor to carry that risk for IP.

We're prepared to share purchase volumes and a shortened SOW for Order Form 1234 if that helps with underwriting. For speed, Tom Harris from Acme Legal is on copy and we can schedule a quick call with your legal team.

Link to HubSpot deal and the redline are attached. Can you confirm Redwood's position and whether your legal team can accept either an uncapped IP carve-out or a defined exception tied to direct IP damages?

Best,

Sarah — thanks for the flag and the redline. Appreciate the clarity on Acme's risk profile.

I'm looping in Monica from Legal and Markus from Product/Engineering to get a quick legal/technical assessment. A few things to help move this faster:

- Can you share concrete examples of the downstream consequential losses you mentioned (revenues, credits to your customers, regulatory fines)?
- Is Acme open to alternatives such as (a) a higher but finite cap specifically for IP indemnities, (b) an escrow/insurance mechanism, or (c) a stepped exception tied to Verified Incidents only?

From my side, we want to avoid an open-ended uncapped exposure. That said, we recognize IP risk is sensitive and are willing to discuss a narrowly-tailored carve-out for proven third-party claims. Monica — can you take first pass on acceptable contract language and whether a $5M / 3x annual fees bucket or insurance requirement is a reasonable compromise?

Rafael / Monica / Markus —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. For context, we had an incident last year at a different vendor where a downstream customer asserted a patent claim that led to multi-month remediation and lost contracts; Acme ultimately paid settlement and sustained material reputational harm. We're trying to avoid that outcome here.

From our redline (see attached) our baseline ask is:

1) IP Indemnity carve-out: Redwood's indemnity for third-party claims of intellectual property infringement shall not be subject to the general limitation of liability.
2) Remedies: The indemnified party may recover amounts awarded by a court and any directly related consequential damages, including documented lost revenues and reasonable mitigation costs.
3) Defense control: Redwood may assume defense, but settlement requires Acme's prior written consent (not to be unreasonably withheld).

If a fully uncapped position is a non-starter, please propose a concrete numerical cap and whether Redwood will accept a limited carve-out for statutory or court-awarded damages. We have a DocuSign link for the Order Form once we align on the MSA language.

Regards,
Tom Harris
Associate General Counsel, Acme

Date: Tue, 21 Apr 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: MSA redlines — IP infringement liability exception

Tom / Sarah —

Thanks for the background and for surfacing Acme's redlines. I've reviewed the requested carve-out and discussed with our leadership. Below is Redwood's counterproposal intended to balance Acme's risk concerns with Redwood's enterprise underwriting and product exposure.

Key points of Redwood's position:

1) IP Indemnity: Redwood will indemnify Acme for third-party claims alleging infringement of a third party's patents, copyrights, or trade secrets arising from use of the Licensed Models as provided in Section X. The indemnity will cover (a) amounts finally awarded by a court; (b) amounts agreed in settlement (with Redwood's prior written consent); and (c) reasonable attorneys' fees and defense costs.

2) Carve-out to Cap: Rather than an uncapped indemnity, Redwood proposes the following limited carve-out: amounts payable under the IP indemnity for a single claim shall not be subject to the general limitation of liability up to an additional IP-specific cap of $10,000,000 (ten million USD). Amounts in excess of $10,000,000 would be subject to mutual senior executive review and will be considered on a case-by-case basis.

3) Consequential Damages: We cannot accept broad recovery of consequential damages for IP claims. Redwood will agree to direct, documented losses reasonably foreseeable and causally linked to the infringement (e.g., documented lost revenue directly caused by an adjudicated infringement), but not indirect or speculative consequential losses (e.g., loss of future business, reputational harm).

4) Injunctive Relief: Both parties retain the right to seek equitable relief (injunctive/declaratory) without waiving other remedies.

5) Mitigations & Controls: Redwood will commit to reasonable mitigation steps on notice of an IP claim (e.g., work to obtain license, make good-faith design-around, temporary mitigation steps). We are open to discussing insurance (e.g., vendor IP insurance) or an escrow arrangement for high-risk SOWs where source exposure is significant.

6) Contractual Wording: Attached is draft counter-language that (a) narrows the carve-out to the IP indemnity; (b) defines recoverable amounts; and (c) sets the $10M IP-specific cap per claim (see Redwood_counter_IP_clause_2026-04-21.docx).

We believe this preserves Acme's ability to recover meaningful losses for proven IP claims while limiting open-ended exposure for Redwood. If Acme insists on recovery of broad consequential damages, Redwood will need to require (i) material premium adjustments or (ii) mandatory vendor IP insurance with predefined limits.

Next steps: if the $10M IP carve-out is acceptable in principle, Rafael and I can incorporate the language into the MSA and push to Order Form signature. If not, can Acme propose a concrete alternative (specific dollar cap or insurance requirement) so we can get procurement to close this week?

Regards,
Monica Patel
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com
Attachment: Redwood_counter_IP_clause_2026-04-21.docx
